text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnia's ruling parties, Party of Democratic Action (SDA) and Croat Democratic Union (HDZ), fail to appoint the president of the federation and his deputy "although a compromise on this issue can be reached", says Halid Genjac, the head of the main SDA board in Sarajevo.
- U.S. non-governmental organisation World Vision will repair 50 private houses in the Sarajevo suburb of Ilijas.

- Bosnia's collective presidency has yet to appoint new ambassadors. The highest priority for appointments will be for the seven most industrialised countries, Russia, Croatia and Serbia, said Jadranko Prlic, foreign minister.
- A clinic for children and students in the Sarajevo suburb opened on Wednesday thanks to funds provided by the Japanese governement and the World Health Organisation (WHO).
